audience: Engineers new to the proposal-versus-verification distinction.
prerequisites: Autoregressive generation appends tokens from a committed prefix.
objective: Distinguish three serial target calls from one batched target verification in an all-accepted three-token example.
scope: A model/token flow illustration, not a scaled latency diagram, DFlash implementation, rejection algorithm, or generic claim that drafting is parallel.
assumptions: The displayed continuation is can, reason, fast and all candidates are accepted.
Target-call counters count target calls only, not drafting work.
No algorithm timing is measured or drawn to scale here. Standard sequential drafting and DFlash block drafting must not be conflated.
The independent cost example below is explicitly a counterexample for transfer, not scene data or a benchmark.
unknowns: Original narration at indices four and five describes a generic drafter as one parallel proposal. That is not established for standard speculative decoding; those blocks are unmapped pending correction.
The final speedup narration lacks explicit costs. Call-count reduction alone does not establish latency improvement.
No runtime event IDs, audiovisual review, or learner responses are supplied.

beats.purpose: Establish a target pass before each new token.

narration.text: A large language model normally generates one token, then waits for the next expensive pass.

beats.purpose: The first target call emits can.
The second target call emits reason.
The third target call emits fast.
Distinguish one batched verification call from three serial target calls without certifying latency.

narration.text: The target verifies the whole batch in one pass. Same target model. Fewer serial waits.

transfer_questions.question: If one verification call replaces three target calls, must the total latency be lower?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: No. With target cost one, three sequential draft steps costing 0.8 each, and verification cost one, speculation takes 3.4 versus 3 baseline units despite all three tokens being accepted.
transfer_questions.justification: Add all work on the critical path: 3 times 0.8 plus 1 = 3.4. A count of target calls omits drafting costs; the independent cost check supplies a counterexample.

transfer_questions.question: Does the horizontal distance between model boxes represent elapsed inference time?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: Not in this flow diagram. It shows data flow and target-call counts; a latency claim requires an explicitly shared clock and overhead model.
transfer_questions.justification: The scene uses fixed model-box positions and arrows without time-valued intervals. The separate ToyTiming example derives completion from explicit costs, which cannot be recovered from those box distances.
